findings.reason: the followup instructs one batch dispatch of every implementable section, so an `§31` node would start on a tree holding neither the test file it must add cases to nor the module it must repair, and would either re-implement `§4`'s decision raiser (two implementations of one mechanism, and a merge conflict against `§4`'s own node) or fail its gate; declaring `"s31": ["…#s4"]` and adding `§31` to the followup's wait list fixes the dispatch, and the section's opening sentence should say `§4`'s run was reviewed rather than landed so the premise matches the plan's own state.
findings.text: `§31` is written against work that is not on the primary branch and declares no wait on it: `§4` is declared `implementable` at `:24`, its commits `e4eef604f4`/`d18e8046fe` are an ancestor of no ref (`git branch -a --contains d18e8046fe` empty, `git merge-base --is-ancestor` against `f38b5cd918` false), `tests/test_a_lost_sessions_work_is_raised.py` and `reckon/crew/lost_session_work.py` are both absent at `f38b5cd918`, and neither `plan-section-depends-on` nor the followup at `:303` ("the other sections are independent") records that `s31` waits on `s4`.

findings.reason: one of the five reviewed gaps is unmeasured, so the gate cannot show it was addressed; naming a search of the repaired module for section labels, and requiring it to return none, gives the deliverable the case it is missing.
findings.text: `§31`'s third deliverable sentence, that the source names its mechanism and no plan section, repairs the fifth cited gap ("a docstring names plan sections") but the done-when asserts only the four added cases, none of which reads the docstring, so a node can pass its gate with the plan labels still in the source.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: the test file `§31` names at `:276` resolves only at `§4`'s unlanded head `d18e8046fe` and not at this revision — the same defect as the wiring finding; the "decision error record the sibling answers return" does resolve, to the `{"ok": false, "error": "decision_error", "detail": …}` record `crew decision record` and `crew decision answer` emit (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:602`), and `lead_decisions.validate_decision` exists at `:88` for the first case to call.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — `§31`'s third deliverable sentence ("The source names its mechanism and no plan section") repairs one of the five cited gaps and is measured by none of the four added cases at `:276`.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate is a repository test file and the node's evidence lands on its own run record; no scratchpad or node-local temporary path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `§31` carries no plan label, ticket number or version tag into a symbol, comment or file name, and its deliverable requires the source to name the mechanism instead of the section.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — each of `§31`'s five stated gaps maps one-to-one onto the five findings recorded in the review at `:485` (store owner and request identity, adopt of a non-live session, traceback on a vanished run, landing untested through the lander, plan labels in a docstring), and each stated cause matches the cited record; the section's "§4 landed" premise does not, and is reported as the wiring finding.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — all four added cases repair the one decision mechanism `§4` delivered (record, answer, landing skip) inside one module set and one test file, so one verdict closes it; the lander case reads `§4`'s own landing skip rather than adding a second capability.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — `s31` adds cases to `tests/test_a_lost_sessions_work_is_raised.py`, the test file `§4` delivers, and `plan-section-depends-on` at `docs/plans/work-of-a-lost-session-is-raised-not-left.html:23` declares no wait for it while the followup at `:303` still calls the remaining sections independent.
